answer: An agent marketplace weights governance votes by escrowed collateral, not account count, and locks that collateral for 30 days after each vote. Splitting one deposit among a tide of fake agents creates no extra voting power: each identity carries only its share. To turn a ripple of influence into control, an attacker must acquire and immobilize a large fraction of the staked asset. A fresh identity is no pearl; scarce capital buys influence.
